AfterCardEnteredCombat.issue: RE-EXECUTED 2026-07-30: the record's filed rationale no longer matches the code and was corrected by re-reading SmoggyPower.cs and the current powers.py directly, rather than re-derived from the stale prose. The stale claim was that this hook walks `getattr(self.owner, 'all_cards', ())` -- it does not, and never plausibly could: `on_card_entered_combat` (powers.py:2090-2096) receives a single `card` argument and reads only `self._skill_played_this_turn`, `card.affliction` and `self._is_skill(card)`. The all_cards/Play-pile-limbo shape described belongs to a DIFFERENT hook on this same power, `AfterCardPlayed`'s sweep (powers.py:2081-2088), which this record already carries as a separate, unqualified `faithful` entry -- so that theory does not support a gap on THIS key. RE-DERIVED FROM SmoggyPower.cs:39-45 (`AfterCardEnteredCombat`) directly: C# guards on `CombatManager.Instance.History.CardPlaysStarted.Any(e => e.HappenedThisTurn(...) && e.CardPlay.Card.Type == Skill && e.CardPlay.Card.Owner.Creature == base.Owner)` -- a HISTORY query, seeded the moment a play STARTS (CardModel.cs:1930, before `OnPlay` runs). The sim instead reads `self._skill_played_this_turn`, a private flag set at powers.py:2085 INSIDE `on_card_played`/AfterCardPlayed -- i.e. AFTER the triggering Skill's own `on_play` has already returned (combat.py:904 dispatches `on_card_played` post-resolution). This is the same HISTORY-vs-FLAG shape already named on this batch's sibling `power/ringing`'s `ShouldPlay` entry (`combat.history` vs a boolean set post-resolution) -- not the pile-limbo class, PROMPT.md bug class 7's cousin instead. OBSERVABLE: if the FIRST Skill a Smog'd player plays this turn generates a new Skill mid-resolution (before its own AfterCardPlayed fires), C# afflicts the new Skill with Smog (its own play-started row already exists in History) and the sim does not (`_skill_played_this_turn` is still False), so the sim's freshly-generated Skill is playable this turn where the game's is blocked. TRIGGER, EXECUTED: `DiscoveryCard` (cards/colorless_skills.py:221-249) is a registered, ported Ironclad Skill (Uncommon, 1E, `card_type = CardType.SKILL`) whose `on_play` synchronously calls `CardPileCmd.add_to_hand(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, card)` (:249) for a card chosen from a 3-option pool draw that can itself be a Skill; `CardPileCmd.add_to_hand` (cmds.py:978-992) calls `_enter_combat` (:992), which fires `hooks.on_card_entered_combat(card)` (cmds.py:878) -- all synchronously inside Discovery's own `on_play`, strictly before Discovery's own `on_card_played` sets the flag. So: Living Fog applies Smoggy to the player, the player's first Skill play this turn is Discovery, and Discovery's 3-option draw offers (and the player picks) a Skill -- a normal, reachable in-run sequence. FIX: replace the `self._skill_played_this_turn` read in `on_card_entered_combat` with a `combat.history.of_type(CardPlayStartedEntry, this_turn=True)` query filtered to `CardType.SKILL` and this power's owner, mirroring `NostalgiaPower.modify_card_play_result_pile`'s already-ported use of the identical API (powers.py:4148-4159, `combat.history.of_type(CardPlayStartedEntry, this_turn=True)`). RADIUS: the private `_skill_played_this_turn` flag is also read by `before_side_turn_start` (reset) and `after_player_turn_end` (reset) -- both are turn-boundary resets, unaffected by this fix -- and by nothing else, so swapping only the `on_card_entered_combat` read to the history query does not disturb `AfterCardPlayed`'s sweep or `ShouldPlay`.

Unlike power/ringing's ShouldPlay, the flag and the history agree here: this hook fires when a card ENTERS combat, never from inside the triggering Skill's own resolution, so the start-vs-finish difference cannot bite. Recorded as a divergence rather than faithful because it is the same substitution that IS observable on power/ringing, and a reader comparing the two should see that the difference is the call site, not the technique.
